page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and dual-socket Intel Xeon 8375C processors running up to 3.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 128 dedicated virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache per socket and instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource allocation features 2048 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture incorporates 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps, eliminating typical cloud bandwidth bottlenecks for high-throughput network and data transmission.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded execution and data throughput. The instance scored within the top 10 percent on the PassMark CPU benchmark, including extended instructions and encryption tests, while multi-core stress-ng tests placed in the top 25 percent. In memory-intensive workloads, the system reached 330 GB/s in large-block read memory bandwidth and executed 105.14 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core scores across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle tier, and CPU-based LLM text generation shows lower throughput on large 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators.

The x2idn.32xlarge is cost-efficient for extreme memory density and consolidated footprint deployments that demand integrated high-speed local NVMe storage without relying solely on remote network volumes. Tradeoffs include modest per-core clock performance relative to compute-specialized types and lower efficiency for token-generation artificial intelligence workloads. It is structured primarily for large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis, real-time analytics, big data processing engines, and memory-bound transactional databases.

Powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors operating at 3.5 GHz, it supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores, paired with 2048 GB of DDR4 memory and 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network performance reaches 100 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the platform places in the top tier for PassMark CPU encryption and extended instruction tests, and achieves top 25 percent results in multi-core compute, database operations, and large-block memory read bandwidth of 330 GB/s. The instance delivers high resource density for workloads constrained by memory capacity and local I/O throughput, making it appropriate for large-scale in-memory databases, electronic design automation, enterprise data analytics, and real-time cache layers.
